what: The cooperative sampler, working: armed across AT&T8 with no reset, and it captured traffic
board: 20.16 MHz Courier V.Everything, ID_SDL v4.03d, supervisor 7.4.16, DSP 3.1.2
the combination that works: Timer 0's vector, which &T8 does NOT rewrite (unlike INT3's), displacing a handler that is a two-instruction EOI stub - with the sampler placed at 0x1a00, inside the 0x1600-0x2b00 range that &T8 leaves intact. Every earlier failure had one or the other: a vector the firmware repoints mid-run, or a handler sitting in the 0x3000-0x8000 range &T8 zeroes.

result.reset: none - the sentinel at 0xd000 survived and the code at 0x1a00 was intact afterwards
result.ring: filled - 3.2 s of the 8 s run, at timer 0's 200 Hz

captured.0x18: 8 distinct values, 54 transitions: C0 C4 C8 CC CE D8 DC FF

means: This is the first sampling of the ASIC's handshake group on a live board while the firmware is doing something. The idle run (coop-sampler-01) read one constant value per port; here every port moves, and 0x18 in particular walks a repeating pattern. What the values mean is not interpreted here - the run demonstrates that the instrument works under load, which is what four previous builds failed to do.
limits: The ring filled after 3.2 s of an 8 s run. Fewer ports or a buffer in the 0xd000 region would cover a longer event.
&T8 is not a call. A call may touch different RAM and repoint different vectors, so the placement and the vector choice both need re-checking before a call capture is trusted.
Disarm remains mandatory: nothing resets the board when this works.
